name: positive-period-disambiguation
scenario: Positive activation: question entity matches multiple table titles; only temporal granularity discriminates
task: According to the weekly report on Federal Credit Programs, what were the total direct loans for the week ending January 12?
source_data:
TABLE OF CONTENTS
FCP-VI-1 - Federal Credit Programs, Weekly
FCP-VI-2 - Federal Credit Programs, Monthly
FCP-VI-3 - Federal Credit Programs, Quarterly

[FCP-VI-1 data excerpt]
Week ending Jan 5: Direct Loans $120M, Guarantees $340M
Week ending Jan 12: Direct Loans $155M, Guarantees $290M

[FCP-VI-2 data excerpt]
January: Direct Loans $510M, Guarantees $1,420M

[FCP-VI-3 data excerpt]
Q1: Direct Loans $1,560M, Guarantees $4,100M
expected_behavior: Skill activates. All three FCP-VI tables share the same entity name ('Federal Credit Programs') and differ only by temporal granularity. Agent must match 'weekly' in the question to FCP-VI-1 (Weekly), not FCP-VI-2 (Monthly) or FCP-VI-3 (Quarterly). Agent names 'Table FCP-VI-1 - Federal Credit Programs, Weekly' before extracting.
regression_guard: Agent must not pick FCP-VI-2 or FCP-VI-3 and report $510M or $1,560M, which use the wrong temporal granularity despite sharing the same entity name.

name: negative-row-entity-not-table-entity
scenario: Negative no-activation: question entity is a row-level lookup key, not a table-title entity
task: What were Brazil's total exports according to the trade data?
source_data:
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Table 1 - International Merchandise Trade by Country, 2020
Table 2 - Trade in Services by Category, 2020

[Table 1 data excerpt]
Country      Exports ($B)   Imports ($B)
United States   1,430       2,340
China           2,590       2,060
Germany         1,670       1,180
Brazil            230         178
Japan             690         650

[Table 2 data excerpt]
Category           Exports ($B)
Transportation      1,040
Travel                680
Financial Services    420
expected_behavior: Skill does not activate. 'Brazil' is a row entity within Table 1, not a table-level title entity. The question does not describe the data source using a report/trust-fund/program/entity-type name that matches formal table titles. The agent identifies 'International Merchandise Trade by Country' as the relevant table through normal contextual reasoning (a country is merchandise trade, not a services category), not by matching 'Brazil' against table titles.
regression_guard: Skill must not activate when the entity in the question (Brazil) is a row value, not a table-title match candidate. The matching procedure would be a category error.

name: positive-ambiguous-near-duplicate-titles
scenario: Positive activation: two tables share an entity name and differ only by a sub-qualifier in the title
task: For the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund, what were the total receipts from operations in fiscal year 1993?
source_data:
TABLE OF CONTENTS
GA-III-4a - Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund: Income from Operations
GA-III-4b - Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund: Investment Holdings
GA-III-5 - Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund

[GA-III-4a data excerpt]
FY 1993: Payroll Taxes $72.3B, Premiums $18.9B, Interest $7.0B, Total Receipts $98.2B

[GA-III-4b data excerpt]
FY 1993: Treasury Securities $132.4B, Agency Bonds $15.6B, Total Holdings $148.0B

[GA-III-5 data excerpt]
FY 1993: Total Receipts $32.1B
expected_behavior: Skill activates. Both GA-III-4a and GA-III-4b share 'Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund' in their titles. Agent must match the question's 'receipts from operations' to GA-III-4a 'Income from Operations', not GA-III-4b 'Investment Holdings' and not GA-III-5 (wrong trust fund entirely). The qualifier 'operations' / 'Income from Operations' must be used to disambiguate.
regression_guard: Agent must not pick GA-III-4b (same trust fund, wrong sub-table) or GA-III-5 (wrong trust fund entirely). The presence of '$32.1B' in GA-III-5 is a deliberate trap — it matches the 'Total Receipts' concept but for the wrong trust fund.

name: negative-single-table-deceptive-toc
scenario: Negative no-activation: single data table embedded in a document whose section headers resemble a table-of-contents
task: What was the net profit margin reported in the quarterly results? This is the only financial data table in the document. Prefer the table whose title and period match the question over nearby summary tables.
source_data:
ACME CORP QUARTERLY REPORT

TABLE OF CONTENTS
Section 1 - Executive Summary............................2
Section 2 - Revenue Breakdown by Product.................4
Section 3 - Operating Expenses by Department.............6
Section 4 - Consolidated Income Statement................8
Section 5 - Risk Factors................................11

--- Section 4 excerpt ---
CONSOLIDATED INCOME STATEMENT (Q1 2025)
Revenue: $4,250,000
COGS: $2,850,000
Gross Profit: $1,400,000
Operating Expenses: $820,000
Net Income: $580,000
Net Profit Margin: 13.6%
expected_behavior: Skill does NOT activate. Despite: (a) the document having a TOC with numbered sections that could be mistaken for 'named data tables,' (b) the question describing 'quarterly results' as an entity descriptor, and (c) the prompt explicitly saying 'prefer the table whose title and period match' — there is only ONE data table in the document (the income statement). The TOC describes document sections, not multiple competing data tables. The fast-path skip for single-table documents must apply.
regression_guard: The prompt includes the activation trigger phrase 'prefer the table whose title and period match the question over nearby summary tables,' but the skill must NOT activate because there is only one data table. The TOC entries are not data tables — they are document sections. A brittle keyword-matcher might activate on the trigger phrase + TOC, skip the single-table fast-path check, and wastefully iterate through section headers that aren't tables.
